query: For the paper "Offensive Language Identification in Greek" (arXiv: 2003.07459), answer this question: Did they use crowdsourcing for the annotations?

drafts: Yes. The tweets were manually annotated by a team of volunteers through an annotation platform [4], which amounts to crowdsourced-style manual annotation. Inter-annotator agreement was calculated, with 100% agreement labels accepted and majority agreement above 66% used in cases of disagreement [6].

cited_sources.text: 5. Conclusion This paper presented the Offensive Greek Tweet Dataset (OGTD), a manually annotated dataset for offensive lan- guage identiﬁcation and the ﬁrst Greek dataset of its kind. The OGTD v1.0 contains a total of 4,779 tweets, encom- passing posts related to an array of topics popular among Greek people (e.g. political elections, TV shows, etc.). Tweets were manually annotated by a team volunteers through an annotation platform.

Inter-annotator agreement was subsequently calculated and labels with 100% agree- ment were deemed acceptable annotations. In cases of dis- agreement, labels with majority agreement above 66% were selected as the actual annotations of the tweets in ques- tion. For labels with complete disagreement between anno- tators, one of the authors of this paper reviewed the tweets with two extra human judges, to get the desired majority agreement above 66%.
